summary: Anonymous candidate T01/B passes the frozen source-fidelity review and is reader-eligible. All 3 paragraphs were reviewed. No necessary repair was identified; retain the version. Native quantitative feedback is not yet attached. Its later model scores must remain separate from fidelity and reader quality.

document_analysis.structure: P1 starts with the same lamp/chair example and puts specialist availability immediately after it. It then combines bench count and capacity limitation. P2 and P3 retain the source progression from owner approval to a bounded communication proposal.
document_analysis.reasoning_specificity: All numbers, times, mechanisms, labels, and limitations survive. The work required partly determines the queue and arrival time is not the only consideration preserve the original partial rule. Does not necessarily mean it has been neglected preserves uncertainty.
document_analysis.voice_consistency: The explanatory voice is calm and slightly more conversational through contractions. It remains appropriate for a general public audience without becoming jokey or assigning blame.
document_analysis.rhythm_repetition: P1 groups the bench count with what an empty bench does not imply. P2 carries the owner wait and its invisibility in a single linked sentence. This makes the explanation flow smoothly without suppressing any qualification.
document_analysis.language_features: The paraphrases are idiomatic and clear. Capacity is an appropriate ordinary term here. The contractions do not change confidence, instruction strength, or agency. No colloquial phrase jars with the genre.
document_analysis.citations_provenance: The fictional workshop is still expressly fictional. No citation or purported observation is added. Candidate identity and method are unknown; natural phrasing does not establish human origin.

spans.quote: At the fictional Bell Street Repair Room, a lamp may sit on the shelf waiting for the electrical volunteer while a chair brought in later goes straight to someone who works with wood. Only one volunteer handles electrical faults, and she comes on alternate Saturdays. The workshop has four benches, but an empty one doesn't always mean there's capacity for another job. The work required partly determines the queue; arrival time isn't the only consideration.

original_anchor.quote: An empty bench does not always mean a repair workshop can take another job. At the fictional Bell Street Repair Room, there are four benches, but only one volunteer handles electrical faults. She comes on alternate Saturdays. A lamp waiting for her may therefore stay on the shelf while a chair, brought in later, goes straight to someone who works with wood. The queue is organized partly by the work required, rather than simply by arrival time.

candidate_anchors.quote: At the fictional Bell Street Repair Room, a lamp may sit on the shelf waiting for the electrical volunteer while a chair brought in later goes straight to someone who works with wood. Only one volunteer handles electrical faults, and she comes on alternate Saturdays. The workshop has four benches, but an empty one doesn't always mean there's capacity for another job. The work required partly determines the queue; arrival time isn't the only consideration.

proposition_checks.constraint: An empty bench does not always indicate capacity to take another repair.
Bell Street Repair Room is explicitly a fictional example.
Only one volunteer handles electrical faults, and she attends on alternate Saturdays.
A lamp can wait for that volunteer while a later-arriving chair is handled by a wood-working volunteer.
The queue is organized partly by required work rather than solely by arrival time.

speech_act_checks.constraint: Explain a possible mechanism; do not imply all workshops follow this system.
Retain the possibility in the lamp/chair example rather than guaranteeing every such ordering.

full_constraint_coverage.reason: Candidate P1 retains every quantitative and causal detail. Doesn't always and partly retain the source limitations.

original_anchor.quote: There is another pause that visitors cannot easily see. Volunteers need an owner's agreement before buying a replacement part. Until the owner replies, a repair may be ready to continue but unable to move forward. Calling that job unfinished is accurate; calling it neglected may not be.

candidate_anchors.quote: Volunteers also need the owner's agreement before buying a replacement part. A repair may be ready to continue and still have to wait for that reply, a pause visitors cannot easily see. The job is unfinished, but that doesn't necessarily mean it's been neglected.

proposition_checks.constraint: Some pauses are not visible to visitors.
Volunteers require the owner's agreement before purchasing a replacement part.
A repair may otherwise be ready to continue but wait for the owner's reply.
Such a repair can accurately be called unfinished; it is not necessarily neglected.

speech_act_checks.constraint: Qualify the inference from delay to neglect, without asserting that neglect never occurs.
Do not assign fault to all owners or imply they must buy parts themselves.

full_constraint_coverage.reason: Candidate P2 preserves the same approval condition and modal possibility. Doesn't necessarily mean it's been neglected is equivalent to may not be accurate to call it neglected.
